findings_not_failures.finding: layout's Adobe paragraph composer aborts the process on depth, with no typed refusal. adobe_composer.rs paragraph() on ragged text sets the window to the whole paragraph (ragged_depth 0, depth = items + 1) and best() recurses once per line. In a 2 MiB test thread, debug build: 'H LS*2000 I', '(a LS)*2000' and plain wrapped text of 3000 words all end in STATUS_STACK_OVERFLOW (0xC00000FD); Limits.max_lines does not guard it because the recursion runs before any line is counted. The cost is also steep: 600 plain words take 31 s, 1800 words exceed the 120 s test cap. Pre-existing: on the sources of 96ace3ca '(a LS)*2000' and the 3000-word text abort the same way; 'H LS*2000 I' did not, only because the failure R55 recorded collapsed it to two lines, so the correct fix made that shape reach the same limit. The lane declared this UNVERIFIED in notes.open_r55; it is now verified. First-fit, Knuth-Plass and the single-line composer answer typed at every count (90000 lines in under 0.4 s; 100501 lines BudgetExceeded). Reachable from document data: a paragraph style with composition_scope every_line selects this composer (typeset.rs:317). The native fixture host stops at its 4096-byte Type budget (Budget refusal at 1365 breaks; 1000 pass), the Viewer's Type limit is 8192 bytes and layout_ui composes first-fit, so these stay below the abort; a host with a larger Type budget does not. Which host that is: NOT_INSPECTED beyond these. Release build not measured.
findings_not_failures.repair_direction: compose iteratively or bound the window on ragged text; typed budget refusal; a bounded-count test per composer
